definition: Movement learning is learning a skill through practicing and understanding the body movements needed to perform it correctly. In the context of handwriting, it refers to learning the movement patterns for forming and linking letters when writing.

reasons: The packet does not define “movement learning” as a general process of learning any skill through practicing and understanding body movements; it only mentions that “movement learning becomes more valuable” in the specific context of children learning cursive writing and connecting letters.

The handwriting-specific gloss goes beyond the source by stating that movement learning refers to learning movement patterns for forming and linking letters; the packet says letters were taught by demonstrating correct writing movements, but it does not define the term in that way.

The packet supports that cursive handwriting instruction used demonstrations of “correct writing movements” and is based on the idea that “movement learning” becomes more valuable when children connect letters, but it does not explicitly support the definition’s phrasing that movement learning is “learning a skill through practicing and understanding the body movements needed to perform it correctly.” In particular, the packet does not clearly substantiate the component of “understanding the body movements.”
